rationale: A wins because it understands the real story is conditional on proof and builds reporter-shaped paths instead of pretending the seed round is enough. A's "Verdano's three utility pilots are the story its funding round isn't" is the right instinct, with the caveats in plain view; B's "No angle can stand on this until a utility is named and a result exists" throws away the best trade hook instead of sharpening it. B also invents "someone who ran systems inside Tesla Energy," which is credential inflation in a decent suit.
gaps_in_A: "Ex-Tesla Energy and NREL engineers are betting community solar breaks the grid before rooftop does" drags rooftop solar into the headline with no support from the update.
"the community-solar bottleneck is software, not panels" is a useful thesis, but it is still a thesis; the update does not prove panels or finance are no longer the constraint.
"Community solar creates real feeder-level headaches for the utility" is plausible beat knowledge, but it needs sourcing before it becomes a pitch claim.
gaps_in_B: "someone who ran systems inside Tesla Energy" invents a role. The update only says ex-Tesla Energy, not what the founder did there.
"Community-solar grids are hitting a load-balancing wall" states a market condition the update does not prove.
"software is the cheap fix being tried" adds an economic claim with no cost evidence, no comparison to grid upgrades, and no independent results.
"No angle can stand on this until a utility is named and a result exists" is too absolutist; a named pilot buyer or procurement-story path could still be real trade press material.
